spiritual well-being and pain interference are both associated with depression in persons with MS, and these relationships appear to be reciprocal.

pain, depression, and spiritual well-being are related to each other in a complex manner.
spiritual well-being and pain are both related to depressive symptoms.
pain, spiritual well-being, and depression are interrelated in patients with MS, but the relationships are complex and require further investigation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
spiritual well-being is an important component of the overall quality of life of individuals with multiple sclerosis.
pain, depression and spiritual well-being are interrelated and should be considered together in treatment.

the spiritual domain is an important aspect of well-being that is not adequately captured by measures of psychological health and should be considered when assessing the well-being of patients with MS and other chronic illnesses.
